claim: The Park Service boundary study says that the historic Hospital Woods are all that remain of the site of Camp Letterman, the U.S. General Hospital for about 5,000 Union and Confederate troops wounded at Gettysburg.

source.edition: Boundary Study, Gettysburg National Military Park: Draft Report to Congress / Environmental Assessment (1988 (the cover letter date is illegible in the text layer; the listing and file name say 1988))

quote: These historic woods are all that remain of the site of Camp Letterman, the U.S. General Hospital for about 5,000 Union and Confederate troops wounded at Gettysburg.

data.name: Camp Letterman, the U.S. General Hospital

value.unit: wounded troops of both armies the hospital was for (about)

notes: the heading of the entry reads HOSPITAL WOODS (11 ACRES); the quote starts after it

claim: The Park Service teachers' guide says Camp Letterman, a general hospital for the wounded who could not yet travel, was created and did not close for over four months.

source.edition: Care of the Wounded Student Program: Teachers' Guide (not stated)

quote: Camp Letterman, a general hospital for the wounded who could not yet travel, was created, and did not close for over four months.
notes: no date is printed: the opening (20 or 22 July) and closing (20 November or January) dates are to be found in other sources and carried as conflicts

claim: Cuyler writes that those obliged to remain will be quartered in a large field hospital established at a suitable place near the town.

source.edition: War of the Rebellion: Official Records, Series I, volume 27, parts 1 to 3, Washington: Government Printing Office, 1889; report ids and printed pages: docs/battle-theatre/library/or27_index.json
source.part: OR27-1-R003 Report of Medical Inspector John M. Cuyler, Washington, D. C., July 27, 1863

quote: Those who are obliged to remain will be quartered in a large field hospital established at a suitable place near the town
notes: the report does not name Camp Letterman; the identity with the general hospital on the York Pike rests on the date and the description and is a row of kind inferred for the group to write

claim: The surgical history reports that Corporal A. W. McCausland of Company B, 16th Maine, aged 18 years, was wounded at Gettysburg on July 2, 1863, was admitted to the field hospital of the First Corps, and on August 24th was transferred to Camp Letterman.

source.edition: Part III, Volume II, Surgical History, first issue, Washington: Government Printing Office, 1883 (chapters X to XV: lower extremities, miscellaneous injuries, complications, anaesthetics, the medical staff and materia chirurgica, transportation of the wounded)

quote: Corporal A. W. McCausland, Co. B, 16th Maine, aged 18 years, was wounded at Gettysburg, July 2, 1863, and admitted to the field hospital of the First Corps. On August 24th he was transferred to Camp Letterman

data.person: A. W. McCausland (Cpl., Co. B, 16th Maine)
data.wound: flesh wound of the left thigh by a shell
data.outcome: transferred from the First Corps field hospital to Camp Letterman on August 24th
